title: Replying to @mads_966 I’m back in my Hadestown era I fear #Broadway #...
transcript: We have to talk about the new Hadestown cast! Like the Jordan Fisher Orpheus hype is real, but honestly the whole cast: Solea Pfeiffer, Philip Boykin, even Betty Who, Lillis White- everyone is giving such incredible performances! I'll start with Jordan Fisher, cause I think that he might be my favorite Orpheus? I think vocally he sounds incredible, his voice was kind of like a perfect mix between Damon Dauno Orpheus and Reeve Carney Orpheus and acting like he had really great chemistry with Solea. Like you really felt like he was like head over heels in love with this woman and the thing that was holding him back was this lack of self confidence. This feeling of like “I am not worthy of her” and that really worked, especially when you consider how the show ends, like that is a really great take on the role. And speaking of Solea, I was equally obsessed with her Eurydice! her Eurydice has like a grit to it. Like you feel like she's seen some things, and so she starts the show super jaded and you get to see that journey that she goes on where she learns to hope and to see the world as it could be. And for me that journey that Eurydice goes on during the show has never been clearer than it was watching Solea’s Eurydice. And it goes without saying, but like vocally she's incredible! I also wanna talk about Philip Boykin’s Hades, because his Hades was so unexpected to me but I loved his take on the role. He infuses the role with a lot more personality and dynamics than Patrick did, who played the role much more stoically. And it was cool to see Hades with a little bit of a personality, he felt much more grounded than mythic, which I think worked! And then you have Betty Who’s Persephone, which also kind of breaks the mold on what that character is and has been. Her Persephone is like, Rockstar Persephone if that makes sense. For someone who is mostly known for singing, as opposed to acting and performing, I thought she gave a surprisingly great performance! And then you have Lillias White as Hermes, who's been in the role for a little while but I haven't gotten a chance to see her yet. I thought she was fantastic! She doesn't really have the etherealness that Andre had, but she still has that stage presence in that gravitas and she kills this role vocally, like she is adding runs and belts and it's so so impressive! So yeah if you haven't seen Hadestown, or if you saw Hadestown a while ago and haven't been back in a while. this is your sign go see Hadestown again (or for the first time) because what this cast is doing is so incredible!
reasoning: Broadway Ben gives enthusiastic praise for the entire Hadestown cast, calling performances 'incredible' and providing detailed positive analysis of each actor's unique take on their roles. He ends with a clear recommendation to see or re-see the show.
